children.name: Text to Video, Physics and Continuity
children.blurb: Text to video models that generate moving images from natural language prompts, with a focus on physical plausibility and temporal continuity.

children.name: Virtual Camera and Lensing
children.blurb: Virtual camera and lensing in AI video synthesis covers the simulation of camera position, movement, focal length, depth of field, and lens distortion within generated or composited footage.

children.name: Face Replacement and Digital Doubles
children.blurb: Face replacement and digital doubles cover techniques for swapping one person's face onto another performer's body, creating a synthetic likeness of an actor for stunts, de-aging, or posthumous appearances, and generating fully synthetic human faces for background or principal roles.

children.name: Storyboarding and Pre-visualization
children.blurb: AI storyboarding and pre-visualization covers the use of generative image and video models to turn scripts, shot lists, and director's notes into rough visual sequences before production.

children.name: Frame Interpolation and Restoration
children.blurb: Frame interpolation creates intermediate frames between existing frames to increase temporal resolution or smooth motion.

sections.body: Cinematography and video synthesis covers AI systems that generate or alter moving images, from text prompts to full scenes, and the tools that mimic camera work, replace faces, plan shots, and repair footage. In practice, text to video models now produce short clips with coherent motion for simple actions, virtual camera tools let a director move a viewpoint through a generated or captured scene, and face replacement is used for de-aging actors or swapping stunt performers. Storyboarding tools turn written scenes into rough visual sequences, while frame interpolation creates new frames between existing ones to slow motion or raise frame rates. These are working systems, not lab demos, used in advertising, game cinematics, and independent film.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The field is uneven. Text to video can handle a few seconds of plausible motion but often breaks object permanence, lighting, and physical contact, so longer shots still need heavy manual cleanup. Virtual camera and lensing is more mature for static or precomputed scenes, but real time control over generated video remains limited by compute and consistency. Face replacement and digital doubles are reliable for short, controlled shots, yet uncanny movement and legal consent issues persist. Storyboarding and pre-visualization are useful for rough drafts, but they do not replace a trained storyboard artist for nuance. Frame interpolation and restoration are the most settled, with good results for clean footage, though damaged or complex motion still produces artifacts. The site tracks 1000 video models, which shows the volume of activity, but quantity does not equal reliability.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: A reader should start with Text to Video, Physics and Continuity to understand the core generation problem and why motion and object permanence are hard. Virtual Camera and Lensing then explains how AI mimics focal length, depth of field, and camera movement after a scene exists. Face Replacement and Digital Doubles covers the specific task of swapping identities, including the consent and likeness issues that follow. Storyboarding and Pre-visualization moves earlier in the pipeline, showing how AI turns a script into a visual plan before shooting or full generation. Frame Interpolation and Restoration sits at the end, dealing with footage that already exists and needs repair or smoother motion. Together these pages trace a production path from idea to finished frame, with each page addressing a different failure point.
